q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a steel water bottle?
title: Steel water bottle carbon footprint per bottle
short: Weigh each bottle and multiply by the stainless steel supplier's figure, then add the cap. Add deep drawing, welding, polishing and printing energy, then divide the plant's energy by bottles made.
audience: Stainless steel bottle and flask makers

p: Report per bottle by capacity and weight. Stainless steel is usually most of the figure.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per bottle (one month)
lines: Plant total: 28,400 / 60,000 = 0.473 kg CO2 per bottle
Add stainless steel and cap for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
